# DSH WSL Workspace Enhanced
**Run DeepSeek Harness on Windows. Work on your code in WSL.**
English · 简体中文 · Other languages

This repository is an independently maintained **fork** of the original
`dsh-wsl-workspace` project.
**This fork:** https://github.com/yaelysia/dsh-wsl-workspace

DSH keeps its interface, models, sessions and plugin management on Windows. Your project
stays insid

e a local Linux distribution, where DSH uses Linux paths, shell commands,
file editing and code sear
ch. **You do not need to install a second DSH in WSL.**
## What this fork does
| Workflow | How it works |
| Open a Linux project | Choose a WSL distribution, Linux user and directory from the **W** workspac

e entry in DSH |
| Run commands | Use a persistent WSL Bash session; interactive programs can use `w

sl_terminal` |
| Read and edit files | Use normal DSH `read` / `write` / `edit` tools backed by nati

ve Linux file I/O |
| Find code | Use `grep` and `glob` inside the distribution, with reusable searc

h execution |
| Keep Windows access | Reach mounted drives such as `/mnt/c/Users/...` without moving

your project |
| Avoid repeated startup | File and search operations share an owner-scoped RPC work
er when their settings agree; idle workers can be released and recreated |

The emphasis is on a **normal DSH workflow**, not a parallel agent running in Linux.
The file and se

arch backend is designed to keep results, execution identity and workspace
paths consistent across t

designed to keep results, execution identity and workspace
paths consistent across the same session.
## Requirements

- **Windows** with WSL installed and at least one working Linux distribution.
- **DeepSeek Harness f

or Windows**, with third-party plugin installation available.
- **Python 3.8+ inside the distributio
n** (`python3`), used by native file and persistent RPC workers.
Check your environment in Windows PowerShell:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Replace `Ubuntu` with your distribution name. WSL does **not** need another DSH, Node.js,
a pip inst

allation, a background service or an open network port. Node.js 24+ is needed
only when building or
testing this repository as a developer.
## Install
**Pre-release:** distributed through GitHub Releases. The existing behaviour matrix still has three
unresolved items; see release behaviour matrix.

1. Open the **Plugins** page in Windows DSH and select the option to add a third-party plugin.
2. In
stall this release's Git source:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
3. Enable the plugin, then **fully exit and restart DSH** (including its host process).
CLI installation:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

For the development branch, use `git+https://github.com/yaelysia/dsh-wsl-workspace.git#main`.
GitHub

Releases provides versioned downloads.
This enhanced fork is not published to npm.

The upstream npm package named `dsh-wsl-workspace` is **not** this fork. Do not enable
both copies u
nder the same plugin identity. The installed plugin version is declared in `package.json`. For Git i

nstallations,
**also check the Git source and resolved commit SHA** to verify which code was install

allations,
**also check the Git source and resolved commit SHA** to verify which code was installed.
**Updating:** Install the Git source with the new release tag, or keep `#main` to follow the develop

ment branch. If DSH's plugin updater cannot identify an
already-installed Git package, record your s

ettings, remove the old copy through the
plugin manager and install this source again. A full restar

t is the reliable way to
activate changes; live profile reload is controlled by DSH itself. If an up

date reports
failure, verify the installed source/commit before treating it as updated.
## Create your first WSL workspace

1. Click **W** beside Settings in DSH.
2. Select the distribution and, optionally, the Linux usernam

e.
3. Enter a Linux absolute directory, for example `/home/me/projects/demo`.
4. Choose **Create & o
pen**, then select a mode that exposes the tools you need (such as **WSL Standard**).

Try reading a source file, searching for a symbol with `grep`, editing it with `edit`,
and running a

test with `bash`. Normal DSH file tools should be used directly: wrapping
every operation in `wsl.e
xe` or Bash defeats the point of the integration.

**Paths and identity:** Linux files use Linux path semantics, including case sensitivity.
Windows dr

ives remain available at `/mnt/c/...`. File and search workers use the
selected WSL identity; distin

ct workspace owners remain isolated rather than sharing a
global worker. Mode-specific tools, includ
ing background jobs, depend on the chosen DSH mode.

## Compatibility

**Desktop verification:** DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.2 was exercised on Windows/WSL,
including native tool

s, workspace isolation, idle recovery, restart and shared RPC.
The latest shared-pool fix was accept
ed in the user's Desktop verification after PR #7.
